name: Engineering docs
blurb: Technical docs for a software system: tutorials, how-to guides, reference, explanation.
placeholder:
There is an API that receives orders from the web client and saves them in the Postgres database. The API then puts a message on the queue. The worker reads the message and the consumer sends a confirmation email, and then it updates it.

To set up the service, the user should first clone the repo, then run `make dev`, and after that check the DLQ. Restart the worker if the queue is stuck.

stages.label: Tutorial
stages.hint: A lesson: the learner builds something step by step.

stages.label: How-to guide
stages.hint: Steps that solve one specific, real task.

stages.label: Reference
stages.hint: Neutral facts: endpoints, options, limits, error codes.

stages.label: Explanation
stages.hint: Background and reasons: why the system works this way.

sources.title: Diátaxis: a systematic approach to technical documentation authoring
sources.author: Daniele Procida

sources.title: Google developer documentation style guide: Highlights
sources.author: Google

sources.title: Microsoft Writing Style Guide: Top 10 tips for Microsoft style and voice
sources.author: Microsoft

rules.name: One doc, one type
rules.rule: Keep each document to one type: tutorial, how-to guide, reference or explanation. Link to the other types instead of mixing them in.
rules.look_for: Steps interrupted by paragraphs of background, design history or full option tables; reference pages containing procedures.
rules.bad: Run `make dev`. Historically we used Docker Compose because the original team preferred it, and before that Vagrant.
rules.good: Run `make dev`. For why the project uses Make, see About the build system.

rules.name: Title how-tos 'How to'
rules.rule: Title a how-to guide with exactly what it shows, in the form 'How to' plus the task.
rules.look_for: Procedural doc titled with a bare noun phrase or '-ing' phrase: 'Worker deployment', 'Deploying workers'.
rules.bad: Queue worker deployment
rules.good: How to deploy a queue worker

rules.name: Write for the user's goal
rules.rule: Build a how-to guide around a task the user needs done, not around a tool's features or buttons.
rules.look_for: Steps that only narrate obvious tool operations ('click Deploy to deploy') with no stated user goal.
rules.bad: To deploy the configuration, select the options and press Deploy.
rules.good: To keep failed orders for 14 days, set `retention_days: 14` on the dead-letter queue, then deploy.

rules.name: Show the destination
rules.rule: Open a tutorial by saying what the learner will build or achieve.
rules.look_for: Tutorial begins with steps or concepts and never states the finished result up front.
rules.bad: Step 1: Install Redis.
rules.good: In this tutorial we will build an order API that queues confirmation emails. Step 1: Install Redis.

rules.name: Show expected output
rules.rule: After each tutorial step, tell the learner what they should see, with example output where possible.
rules.look_for: A command or action with no following line that shows or describes the expected result.
rules.bad: Run `curl localhost:8080/health`.
rules.good: Run `curl localhost:8080/health`. The API responds with `{"status":"ok"}`.

rules.name: One path in tutorials
rules.rule: In a tutorial, give a single path to the goal; leave options and alternatives for other docs.
rules.look_for: 'Alternatively', 'you could also', 'or, if you prefer' inside tutorial steps.
rules.bad: Install Postgres with Homebrew, or alternatively Docker, or you could also use a managed instance.
rules.good: Install Postgres with Homebrew.

rules.name: Reference only describes
rules.rule: In reference material, state facts about the system neutrally; leave out opinion, marketing and step-by-step instruction.
rules.look_for: Opinion or sales words in reference text ('powerful', 'easy', 'simply'), or procedures mixed into parameter descriptions.
rules.bad: `max_retries` is a powerful option you will love. First open the dashboard, then click Settings.
rules.good: `max_retries`: integer, default 3. Number of times the worker retries a failed job.

rules.name: Explain the why
rules.rule: In explanation, give reasons and context: design decisions, constraints and the alternatives considered.
rules.look_for: Overview lists components but never says why they were chosen or what trade-offs they carry.
rules.bad: The system uses a queue between the API and the worker.
rules.good: The API puts emails on a queue so that a slow mail provider cannot delay order responses.

rules.name: Define new terms
rules.rule: Define each unfamiliar term or acronym where it first appears, or link to a definition.
rules.look_for: Acronym or project-specific term used with no definition or link on first use: 'the DLQ', 'the reaper'.
rules.bad: Failed jobs go to the DLQ.
rules.good: Failed jobs go to the dead-letter queue (DLQ), a queue that holds messages the worker could not process.

rules.name: One name per thing
rules.rule: After you name something, keep using that exact name.
rules.look_for: One component called by several names: 'worker', then 'consumer', then 'job runner'.
rules.bad: The worker reads the queue. The consumer then sends the email.
rules.good: The worker reads the queue. The worker then sends the email.

rules.name: No ambiguous pronouns
rules.rule: Replace any 'it', 'this', 'that' or 'they' that could point at more than one noun.
rules.look_for: A pronoun that follows two or more candidate nouns, so its referent is unclear.
rules.bad: The API sends the job to the queue, and it retries it if it fails.
rules.good: The API sends the job to the queue. If the job fails, the worker retries the job.

rules.name: Prefer active voice
rules.rule: Write in active voice so the reader knows which component performs the action.
rules.look_for: 'is', 'are' or 'was' plus a past participle with no actor: 'the job is retried', 'requests are validated'.
rules.bad: The order is written to the database.
rules.good: The API writes the order to the database.

rules.name: Cut 'there is'
rules.rule: Rewrite sentences that start with 'there is' or 'there are' around a real subject and verb.
rules.look_for: Sentences beginning 'There is', 'There are' or 'There exists'.
rules.bad: There is a worker that processes the queue.
rules.good: A worker processes the queue.

rules.name: One idea per sentence
rules.rule: Limit each sentence to a single idea; split long ones or convert them to lists.
rules.look_for: Sentences with three or more clauses chained by 'and', 'which' or 'but', or running past about 30 words.
rules.bad: The API validates the order and writes it to Postgres, which triggers a message that the worker reads and then emails.
rules.good: The API validates the order and writes it to Postgres. The API then publishes a message. The worker reads the message and sends the email.

rules.name: Number sequential steps
rules.rule: Put steps that must happen in order in a numbered list; use bullets only when order does not matter.
rules.look_for: Ordered steps written as a paragraph ('first… then… after that') or as bullet points.
rules.bad: First clone the repo, then run `make dev`, and after that open the dashboard.
rules.good:
1. Clone the repo.
2. Run `make dev`.
3. Open the dashboard.

rules.name: Start steps with verbs
rules.rule: Begin every numbered step with an imperative verb.
rules.look_for: Numbered steps starting with 'You should', 'The user', 'Next, the' or a noun.
rules.bad: 1. The repo should be cloned by the user.
rules.good: 1. Clone the repo.

rules.name: State scope and audience
rules.rule: Begin the document by stating what it covers, who it is for and its key points.
rules.look_for: Opening paragraph that does not say what the doc covers or who should read it.
rules.bad: Orders are important to our business.
rules.good: This guide shows backend engineers how to run the order service locally. It assumes you have Docker installed.

rules.name: Address the reader as you
rules.rule: Write to the reader as 'you'; do not use 'we' or 'the user' for the reader's actions.
rules.look_for: 'The user should', 'developers must', 'one can', or 'we' for actions the reader performs.
rules.bad: The user should set the API key.
rules.good: Set your API key.

rules.name: Condition before instruction
rules.rule: Put the condition before the instruction it applies to.
rules.look_for: Instruction sentences that end in 'if…', 'when…' or 'unless…'.
rules.bad: Restart the worker if the queue is stuck.
rules.good: If the queue is stuck, restart the worker.

rules.name: Code in code font
rules.rule: Format commands, file names, endpoints, field names and other code-related text as code.
rules.look_for: Commands, paths, endpoints or config keys in plain text or quotation marks instead of backticks.
rules.bad: Run make dev and open config.yaml.
rules.good: Run `make dev` and open `config.yaml`.

rules.name: Don't pre-announce
rules.rule: Document what exists now; leave out announcements of unreleased features.
rules.look_for: 'Coming soon', 'will be supported in a future release', 'we plan to add'.
rules.bad: Batch refunds are coming soon.
rules.good: The API does not support batch refunds.

rules.name: Descriptive link text
rules.rule: Write link text that describes the destination.
rules.look_for: Links labelled 'click here', 'here', 'this page', or a bare URL.
rules.bad: For queue settings, click [here](/reference/queue).
rules.good: See the [queue settings reference](/reference/queue).

rules.name: Lead with the point
rules.rule: Put the most important information first and front-load keywords so readers can scan.
rules.look_for: A document or section opening with history or preamble, with the key action or fact several sentences in.
rules.bad: Over the years many teams have asked about retries. After much discussion, we decided the worker retries three times.
rules.good: The worker retries a failed job three times.

rules.name: Sentence-case headings
rules.rule: Capitalize only the first word and proper nouns in headings.
rules.look_for: Headings In Title Case: 'Getting Started With The Order Service'.
rules.bad: Getting Started With The Order Service
rules.good: Getting started with the order service

rules.name: Use contractions
rules.rule: Use common contractions such as it's, you'll and don't to keep a friendly, natural tone.
rules.look_for: 'Do not', 'it is', 'you will', 'cannot' spelled out throughout where a contraction would read naturally.
rules.bad: You will not need a database for this step.
rules.good: You won't need a database for this step.
